A.note: Best atmosphere: hazy distant hills, believable water gradient with foam and soft light, convincing fortified shoreline. Streets between buildings are a little flat and the ships are tiny.

B.note: Close, high camera. The ground has a noisy white-line pattern that looks like a texture error. The buildings are chunky blocks and the walls are simple. No horizon, so little sense of place.

C.note: Water is saturated, flat swimming-pool blue, and the wide frame is clean. The terrain looks flat and the buildings are boxy. The horizon is crisp but less atmospheric than in A.

D.note: Good haze and depth, and the rendering is natural-looking. The grassy slope in the foreground is a bit bare and the ground is pale and flat. Overall it is less sharp and saturated than A.

why: A has the most convincing atmosphere, water and materials, with the least toy-like feel. B has a noisy ground texture and chunky blocks, and C's water is a flat saturated blue.
top_fix_for_best: Break up the pale, flat ground between the buildings with street texture, shadows, courtyards, gardens and smoke. Add more and larger ships and a few tiny moving figures on the walls and quays, so the scale and a sense of life read on a small screen.
